lorentz-factor-time-dilation.title: Lorentz Factor and Time Dilation
lorentz-factor-time-dilation.meaning: Between the same two events, a moving clock records less elapsed time than clocks in the laboratory frame.
lorentz-factor-time-dilation.conditions: Inertial frames with a constant relative speed |v| < c; Δτ is the time between events in the frame where they occur at the same location.
lorentz-factor-time-dilation.units: γ: dimensionless; v and c: m/s; Δt and Δτ: s

lorentz-transform-interval.title: Lorentz Transformation and Spacetime Interval
lorentz-transform-interval.plain: β = v/c; γ = 1/√(1 − β²); ct′ = γ(ct − βx); x′ = γ(x − βct); Δs² = c²Δt² − |Δr|²
lorentz-transform-interval.meaning: The transformation mixes position and time while preserving the spacetime interval and the causal type of a pair of events.
lorentz-transform-interval.conditions: Inertial frames with parallel axes and relative velocity v along x; β = v/c, the origins coincide at t = t′ = 0, and the (+,−,−,−) metric convention is used.
lorentz-transform-interval.units: ct, x, and |Δr|: m; Δs²: m²; β and γ: dimensionless; t: s

relativistic-energy-momentum.title: Relativistic Energy–Momentum Relation
relativistic-energy-momentum.meaning: The total energy of a free particle is related to its momentum and invariant mass.
relativistic-energy-momentum.conditions: A free particle in special relativity; E includes the rest energy mc².
relativistic-energy-momentum.units: E and mc²: J; p: kg·m/s; m: kg; c: m/s

photon-de-broglie-relations.title: Planck and de Broglie Relations
photon-de-broglie-relations.meaning: Frequency determines a photon's energy, while wavelength determines the momentum of a quantum or a free particle.
photon-de-broglie-relations.conditions: E = hν applies to a photon; λ = h/p is the de Broglie wavelength of a quasi-monochromatic free state.
photon-de-broglie-relations.units: E: J; h: J·s; ν: Hz; p: kg·m/s; λ: m

double-slit-probability.title: Relative Detection Density behind Two Narrow Slits
double-slit-probability.meaning: The squared sum of the amplitudes for two indistinguishable paths produces maxima and minima in the relative density of individual detection events.
double-slit-probability.conditions: Two identical coherent narrow slits in the far field; normalization of the density depends on the chosen angular or screen coordinate. Finite slit width adds a single-slit diffraction envelope, while available which-path information removes the interference term.
double-slit-probability.units: ρ: relative density in the chosen coordinate; d and λ: m; θ: rad

heisenberg-uncertainty.title: Heisenberg Uncertainty Relation
heisenberg-uncertainty.meaning: A quantum state cannot simultaneously have arbitrarily small spreads in position and its conjugate momentum.
heisenberg-uncertainty.conditions: σ_x and σ_p are the standard deviations of measurement outcomes for the same normalized quantum state.
heisenberg-uncertainty.units: σ_x: m; σ_p: kg·m/s; product: J·s

schrodinger-equation.title: Time-Dependent Schrödinger Equation
schrodinger-equation.meaning: It governs the unitary evolution of the wavefunction of a nonrelativistic particle.
schrodinger-equation.conditions: A nonrelativistic spinless particle of constant mass in a scalar potential; ψ must satisfy the boundary conditions and normalization.
schrodinger-equation.units: both sides: J·ψ; ħ: J·s; m: kg; V: J; r: m; t: s

radioactive-decay.title: Law of Radioactive Decay
radioactive-decay.plain: N(t) = N₀e^(−λt); A = λN; T₁/₂ = ln 2 / λ
radioactive-decay.meaning: The number of undecayed nuclei and the activity decrease exponentially when the decay probability is constant.
radioactive-decay.conditions: The nuclei decay independently with a constant λ; the nuclide is neither produced nor subject to changes in its decay channel.
radioactive-decay.units: N: dimensionless; λ: s⁻¹; A: Bq = s⁻¹; T₁/₂ and t: s

nuclear-binding-energy.title: Nuclear Binding Energy
nuclear-binding-energy.meaning: The mass defect between the free nucleons and the nucleus corresponds to the energy required to separate the nucleus into its constituent nucleons.
nuclear-binding-energy.conditions: Consistent ground-state nuclear masses must be used; when using atomic masses, electron masses and their binding energy must be accounted for consistently.
nuclear-binding-energy.units: E_b: J; masses: kg; Z and N: dimensionless; c: m/s

hubble-law.title: Hubble–Lemaître Law
hubble-law.meaning: At low cosmological redshifts, a galaxy's recession speed is approximately proportional to its distance.
hubble-law.conditions: A homogeneously expanding Universe and a sufficiently small redshift; the peculiar velocity must be small compared with H₀d.
hubble-law.units: v: m/s; H₀: s⁻¹; d: m

stellar-hydrostatic-equilibrium.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium of a Star
stellar-hydrostatic-equilibrium.meaning: The pressure gradient supports a spherical star against contraction under its own gravity.
stellar-hydrostatic-equilibrium.conditions: Spherical symmetry, quasistatic Newtonian equilibrium, and negligible rotation; relativistic corrections are required for compact objects.
stellar-hydrostatic-equilibrium.units: P: Pa; r: m; M: kg; ρ: kg/m³; G: m³/(kg·s²)

logistic-map.title: Logistic Map
logistic-map.meaning: This simple nonlinear map exhibits stable points, bifurcations, and chaos as the parameter r changes.
logistic-map.conditions: A dimensionless discrete model; to keep x_n in [0, 1], one usually takes x₀ in [0, 1] and 0 ≤ r ≤ 4.

lyapunov-exponent-map.title: Lyapunov Exponent of a One-Dimensional Map
lyapunov-exponent-map.meaning: A positive exponent indicates exponential divergence of nearby trajectories and sensitivity to initial conditions.
lyapunov-exponent-map.conditions: A differentiable one-dimensional map and a typical, sufficiently long trajectory; when physical time is used, the result is divided by the duration of one time step.

gravitational-constant.name: Gravitational constant
gravitational-constant.note: CODATA 2022; the standard uncertainty is 0.00015e−11 m³/(kg·s²).

reduced-planck-constant.name: Reduced Planck constant
reduced-planck-constant.note: Rounded decimal representation of the exact relation ħ = h/(2π).

elementary-charge.name: Elementary charge
elementary-charge.note: Exact SI defining value; the electron's charge is −e.

vacuum-permittivity.name: Vacuum permittivity
vacuum-permittivity.note: CODATA 2022; since the redefinition of the SI, it is a measured derived quantity.

vacuum-permeability.name: Vacuum permeability
vacuum-permeability.note: CODATA 2022; since the redefinition of the SI, it is no longer exactly equal to 4π·10⁻⁷ N/A².

fine-structure-constant.name: Fine-structure constant
fine-structure-constant.note: CODATA 2022; it characterizes the strength of the electromagnetic interaction.

atomic-mass-constant.name: Atomic mass constant
atomic-mass-constant.note: CODATA 2022; also denoted by u or the dalton (Da).

standard-gravity.name: Standard acceleration due to gravity
standard-gravity.note: Exact conventional value; the local acceleration due to gravity depends on location.

stefan-boltzmann-constant.name: Stefan–Boltzmann constant
stefan-boltzmann-constant.note: Rounded decimal representation of the value derived from the exact c, h, and k_B.

electronvolt-joule.name: Electronvolt in joules
electronvolt-joule.note: Exact conversion: 1 eV is the energy acquired by a charge e when it passes through a potential difference of 1 V.
